title: Spring S1 Quiz Prep: Polynomial Operations
subtitle: Standards S1.a & S1.b · 8 Questions · ~40 min
purpose: Tuesday quiz prep for Kai. S1.a: add and subtract polynomials using function notation (Q1-Q3). S1.b: multiply polynomials (Q4-Q8). Q4 requires showing box method work.

questions.question_html:
Let \( f(x) = 2x^3 - 4x^2 + 3x - 1 \) and \( g(x) = x^3 + 5x^2 - 2x + 4 \).
Find \( f(x) + g(x) \). Write your answer in standard form.
questions.hint: Add like terms for each degree: x³ terms, x² terms, x terms, and constants separately.

questions.question_html:
Let \( f(x) = 3x^3 + 2x^2 - 5x + 1 \) and \( g(x) = x^3 - 4x^2 + 3x - 6 \).
Find \( f(x) - g(x) \). Write your answer in standard form.
questions.hint: Distribute the negative sign to every term of g(x) first, then combine like terms.

questions.question_html:
Simplify. Write your answer in standard form.
\( (3x^3 - 2x^2 + x) + (x^3 + 4x^2 - 5) - (2x^3 - x^2 + 3x - 1) \)
questions.hint: Distribute the negative to the last group first. Then collect x³, x², x, and constant terms.

questions.question_html: Use the box method to multiply \( (3x + 2)(x^2 - 2x + 1) \). Write each factor along the top and side of the box, multiply to fill in all 6 cells, then collect like terms and write your answer in standard form.
questions.hint: Set up a 2×3 box. Top headers: x², -2x, 1. Side headers: 3x, 2. Six interior cells to fill.

questions.question_html:
Multiply. Write your answer in standard form.
\( (3x - 2)(4x + 1) \)
questions.hint: Distribute 3x and -2 across (4x + 1). Combine the x terms.

questions.question_html:
Multiply. Write your answer in standard form.
\( (x + 2)(x^2 - 3x + 5) \)
questions.hint: Distribute x across (x² - 3x + 5), then distribute 2 across (x² - 3x + 5). Combine like terms.

questions.question_html:
Multiply. Write your answer in standard form.
\( (2x - 3)(x^2 + 4x - 1) \)
questions.hint: Distribute 2x and then -3 across the trinomial. Combine the x² terms and the x terms.

questions.question_html: One factor is \( (x + 3) \) and the product is \( x^3 + 5x^2 + 3x - 9 \). Find the missing factor. The leading term \( x^2 \) is given.
questions.hint: Set up the box with x and +3 as your left column headers. Use the product to figure out what goes across the top. Start with the x³ term.
